newsitem.title: USA: FOB Gulf Grain - Corn/soybeans steady, wheat lower.
newsitem.headline: FOB Gulf Grain - Corn/soybeans steady, wheat lower.

text.p: U.S. FOB Gulf corn and soybean offers were steady on Tuesday while hard red winter wheat values dropped, weighed down by a lack of export activity, dealers said.
Demand for HRW wheat was sluggish, one broker said.

Also, high water levels continued to snag barge traffic on the upper Mississippi River. Navigation restrictions remained in place for the port of St. Louis on Tuesday due to high water on the Mississippi there, the U.S. Coast Guard said.
"The safety zone was still in effect until the river at St Louis reaches less than 25 feet," said Lt. Drew Cheney, assistant chief of port operations, Coast Guard Marine Safety Office, St Louis.
Officials said water levels continued to rise in Iowa, Illinois and Missouri along the Mississippi River.
Locks and dams from lower and upper St Anthony Falls, Minn., to Lock and Dam 13, near Fulton, Ill., remained closed. "Lock and Dam 13 was shut down this Sunday due to high water," Cheney said.
Lock and Dam 14 at Pleasant Valley, Iowa, and Lock and Dam 15 at Rock Island, Ill., were expected to close on April 18.
Lock and Dam 16 at Muscatine, Iowa and Lock and Dam 17 at New Boston, Ill., were expected to close on April 16.
Lock and Dam 18 at Gladstone, Ill., was expected to close on April 20 and Lock and Dam 20 at Canton, Mo., on April 18. No plans were set for Lock and Dam 19 at Keokuk, Iowa, Cheney said.
